questions.question: Harappan standardized cubical weighing stones discovered across urban settlements were made almost exclusively of which stone?
options: A) Chert
B) Sandstone
C) Marble
D) Pumice
questions.explanation: Standardized Harappan precision weights were predominantly fashioned from chert stone and followed a binary system at lower denominations.

questions.question: The Moroccan globetrotter Ibn Battuta arrived at the imperial court of Delhi during the reign of which Sultan?
options: A) Alauddin Khalji
B) Muhammad bin Tughlaq
C) Feroz Shah Tughlaq
D) Balban
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta reached Delhi in 1334 during the reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who appointed him as the Qazi of Delhi.

questions.question: In which calendar year did Mahatma Gandhi launch the nationwide Non-Cooperation Movement alongside the Khilafat agitation?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in 1920 following the Nagpur and Calcutta sessions of the Indian National Congress.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: In 1838, which officer of the East India Company mint deciphered the ancient Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts on Mauryan inscriptions?
options: A) Colin Mackenzie
B) Alexander Cunningham
C) John Marshall
D) James Prinsep
questions.explanation: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi in 1838, discovering that inscriptions referring to Piyadassi belonged to Ashoka.

questions.question: According to the classification of eight marriage forms in the Manusmriti, what was the 'Arsha' form of marriage?
options: A) The father gives away his daughter after receiving a cow and a bull from the bridegroom for sacred purposes
B) The bridegroom pays an exorbitant commercial cash bride-price to purchase the bride
C) The bride elopes consensually with her lover without parental knowledge
D) The woman is captured by force from her father's home after killing her relatives
questions.explanation: In the Arsha marriage, the father gave away his daughter after receiving a token pair of cattle from the groom.

questions.question: In Jain philosophy, what is the literal meaning and religious role of a 'Tirthankara'?
options: A) A temple architect who erects towering monolithic pillars of victory
B) A ford-maker or spiritual guide who enables seekers to cross the turbulent river of worldly suffering (samsara)
C) A royal warrior who defends monastic establishments from foreign conquerors
D) An astronomer who computes auspicious dates for royal coronations
questions.explanation: Tirthankaras are ford-makers who pave the path across the ocean of rebirth and transmigration.

questions.question: Which coastal Harappan settlements served as specialized manufacturing centers for shell objects including bangles, ladles, and inlays?
options: A) Kot Diji and Ropar
B) Banawali and Rakhigarhi
C) Nageshwar and Balakot
D) Manda and Alamgirpur
questions.explanation: Nageshwar and Balakot, located near marine shell resources, specialized in creating shell ornaments and implements.

questions.question: The compilation of Kabir's devotional verses preserved and chanted in Rajasthan is titled:
options: A) Bijak
B) Padmavat
C) Sur Saravali
D) Kabir Granthavali
questions.explanation: Verses of Kabir are preserved in three distinct traditions: the Bijak in Varanasi, the Kabir Granthavali in Rajasthan, and the Adi Granth in Punjab.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Which Italian merchant traveler visited the kingdom of Vijayanagara around 1420 during the reign of King Deva Raya I?
options: A) Nicolo de Conti
B) Marco Polo
C) Afanasy Nikitin
D) Fernao Nuniz
questions.explanation: Nicolo de Conti visited Vijayanagara in 1420 and left vivid accounts of the city's fortification walls and festivals.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In the land revenue classification of the Ain-i-Akbari, what was 'Chachar' land?
options: A) Land that yielded two bumper crops every monsoon season without rest
B) Land that had lain fallow for three to four consecutive years before being brought under the plough again
C) Land that had been left uncultivated for five or more years
D) Land reserved solely for imperial royal stables
questions.explanation: Chachar denoted agricultural fields that had remained uncultivated for 3-4 years to recover soil nutrients.

questions.question: Why did Francois Bernier describe major Indian urban centers under the Mughals as 'camp towns'?
options: A) They were fortified solely by temporary canvas tents without stone foundations
B) They were relocated to river islands during the four months of the monsoon
C) He argued they owed their existence and survival entirely to the presence and patronage of the imperial royal court and army
D) They were populated exclusively by foreign mercenary cavalry units
questions.explanation: Bernier characterized Mughal cities as camp towns, asserting they flourished when the court arrived and rapidly declined when it moved.

questions.question: The celebrated 'Fifth Report' on the affairs and administration of the East India Company was submitted to the British Parliament in which year?
questions.explanation: The Fifth Report on East India Company administration in India was placed before the British Parliament in 1813.

questions.question: Lord Dalhousie formally annexed the kingdom of Awadh in February 1856 under which official colonial pretext?
options: A) Alleged gross misgovernance and chronic administrative chaos under Nawab Wajid Ali Shah
B) The lack of a natural biological heir under the Doctrine of Lapse
C) Direct military conspiracy between the Nawab and the Russian Tsar
D) Refusal of the Nawab to pay annual subsidiary military subsidies
questions.explanation: Awadh was annexed in 1856 on charges of misgovernment, deposing Nawab Wajid Ali Shah to the dismay of local taluqdars and sepoys.

questions.question: Which British brigadier-general led the recapture of the city of Delhi from the sepoys in September 1857, suffering mortal wounds during the assault?
options: A) Henry Lawrence
B) John Nicholson
C) Colin Campbell
D) Hugh Rose
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General John Nicholson spearheaded the storming of Delhi in September 1857, where he was fatally wounded near Lahore Gate.

questions.question: Under the terms of the historic Poona Pact concluded in September 1932, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi reached an agreement to:
options: A) Boycott the forthcoming provincial legislative elections under the Government of India Act 1935
B) Establish a sovereign separate administrative territory for Dalits in the Deccan
C) Provide reserved seats for the Depressed Classes within joint electorates rather than creating separate electorates
D) Demand complete immediate independence before addressing caste discrimination
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact replaced separate electorates for Depressed Classes with reserved legislative seats within a general joint electorate.

questions.question: Who presented the resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947 proposing the adoption of the National Flag of India with the Ashoka Chakra?
options: A) Dr. Rajendra Prasad
B) Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
C) Sarojini Naidu
D) Jawaharlal Nehru
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic resolution in July 1947 defining the dimensions, tricolour strips, and navy blue spinning wheel/chakra.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: Sangam poetry celebrates which early Pandya king famous for winning the battle of Talaiyalanganam against a confederacy of Chola and Chera chieftains?
options: A) Nedunjeliyan
B) Karikala
C) Senguttuvan
D) Elara
questions.explanation: Pandya king Nedunjeliyan is celebrated in Sangam literature for his youthful military triumph at Talaiyalanganam.

questions.question: Which major Sufi silsila was introduced in India by Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti when he established his center in Ajmer in the late 12th century?
options: A) Suhrawardi silsila
B) Chishti silsila
C) Naqshbandi silsila
D) Qadiri silsila
questions.explanation: Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti founded the Chishti silsila in northern India, renowned for simplicity, generosity, and musical sama.

questions.question: Which specific paleographic and structural characteristics of the Harappan script have caused it to remain undeciphered by modern linguists?
options: A) It consists of fewer than 20 alphabetic symbols written vertically from bottom to top
B) It is written exclusively on perishable palm-leaf scrolls in Proto-Greek dialects
C) It is logosyllabic with between 375 to 400 signs, written right-to-left, and entirely lacks bilingual inscriptions
D) It was completely erased by Mauryan stone engravers across all settlements
questions.explanation: The script features 375-400 signs, runs generally right-to-left, and has resisted decipherment due to short texts and lack of a bilingual key.

questions.question: In the urban civil engineering of Mohenjodaro, why were sump pits and sedimentation traps installed at periodic intervals along the domestic sewer drains?
options: A) To store drinking water for stray cattle during heatwaves
B) To collect molten copper runoff from household smelting crucibles
C) To capture incoming tidal saltwater for pickling fish
D) To allow solid matter to settle at the base so that only liquid wastewater drained into the covered street channels, facilitating periodic desilting
questions.explanation: Harappan covered drains featured sump pits where solid rubbish deposited, allowing clean drainage and periodic municipal removal.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: The Kushana monarchs of northern India adopted the celestial title 'Devaputra' (son of god) primarily to:
options: A) Project superhuman royal authority and divine legitimation, drawing inspiration from contemporary Chinese emperors ('Son of Heaven')
B) Signify their subjection to Roman Caesars in diplomatic treaties
C) Proclaim their status as mortal disciples of the Jaina Tirthankaras
D) Renounce worldly kingship and transfer imperial revenues to monasteries
questions.explanation: Kushanas assumed titles like Devaputra to project exalted divine legitimacy, matching Chinese imperial traditions.

questions.sub_topic: Political and Economic Systems in Early States
questions.question: According to the account of Megasthenes, the Mauryan military administration in Pataliputra was organized through:
options: A) A hereditary council of four high priests who cast lots before each military expedition
B) A supreme military committee of thirty members subdivided into six specialized boards of five members each
C) Twelve autonomous tribal chieftains who commanded private cavalry squadrons
D) A single supreme commander-in-chief aided solely by Greek mercenary bodyguards
questions.explanation: Megasthenes noted a board of 30 members divided into 6 sub-committees overseeing navy, transport, infantry, cavalry, chariots, and elephants.

questions.question: In the Mahabharata's Dyuta Parva (Gambling Episode), what fundamental legal and moral conundrum does Draupadi present to the elders of the Kuru assembly?
options: A) Whether the dice loaded with lead violated Vedic wagering regulations
B) Whether a woman born of sacrificial fire could be governed by customary marriage laws
C) Whether Yudhishthira, having staked and lost himself first, still possessed legal ownership rights over another person to stake her
D) Whether the game of dice could legally proceed without royal astrologers present
questions.explanation: Draupadi questioned whether Yudhishthira had the legal status to wager his wife after having already forfeited his own liberty.

questions.question: In the Buddhist scripture Sutta Pitaka, the socio-political myth of the 'Mahasammata' explains the genesis of human government through:
options: A) The direct cosmic creation of the four varnas from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet of the divine Purusha
B) A bloody rebellion of outcasts overthrowing a tyrannical oligarchy of forest hermits
C) The divine appointment of a warrior prince through the descent of celestial thunderbolts
D) An elective social contract where people voluntarily surrendered a portion of their paddy to an upright leader to preserve civic order
questions.explanation: The Mahasammata myth explains kingship as a human contract born out of necessity to halt disorder, funded by voluntary taxes.

questions.question: What core doctrinal evolution distinguished the Mahayana concept of the 'Bodhisattva' from earlier Theravada monastic aspirations?
options: A) A Bodhisattva consciously defers personal entry into final nirvana out of boundless compassion to work continuously for the salvation of all beings
B) A Bodhisattva eliminates all emotional attachments by living strictly isolated in mountain caverns
C) A Bodhisattva is required to perform animal sacrifices to ward off evil spirits
D) A Bodhisattva rejects all images and stupa reliquary worship
questions.explanation: Mahayana Bodhisattvas attain immense merit but delay final nirvana to aid all sentient creatures in crossing the ocean of suffering.

questions.question: The magnificent Great Stupa at Amaravati suffered grievous architectural destruction in the 18th and 19th centuries because:
options: A) A catastrophic volcanic eruption submerged the Krishna delta under basaltic lava
B) Local landlords quarried its marble casing for building lime and colonial officers shipped exquisite sculptural panels to museums across Britain and India
C) The stupa was completely dismantled by Ashokan stonecutters to build Nagarjunakonda
D) An earthquake caused the underground limestone caverns beneath the stupa to collapse
questions.explanation: Amaravati was plundered for building material and its exquisite relief slabs dispersed to Madras, Calcutta, and London.

questions.question: How did Al-Biruni intellectually evaluate the rigid Brahmanical theory of inherent ritual pollution and untouchability?
options: A) He fully endorsed the concept as being identical to ancient Persian Zoroastrian purity rites
B) He argued that the system was mathematically necessary to regulate agrarian grain distribution
C) He argued that the conception of absolute permanent impurity was unnatural, noting that natural laws strive to purify corrupted elements, such as sunlight purifying the air
D) He claimed the caste hierarchy was identical to the social stratification of Abbasid Baghdad
questions.explanation: Al-Biruni rejected notions of absolute pollution, stating that in nature, everything that falls into impurity strives to regain its pristine state.

questions.question: According to Ibn Battuta's travelogue, female slaves purchased in the Delhi markets were deployed by Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq specifically for:
options: A) Manning siege engines during border campaigns against the Ilkhanate Mongols
B) Administering provincial treasury departments and revenue audits
C) Conducting theological debates against orthodox ulema in royal mosques
D) Domestic household labour, musical and vocal entertainment, and clandestine espionage to monitor the loyalty of imperial nobles
questions.explanation: Ibn Battuta recorded that the Sultan used female slaves not only for entertainment and domestic work, but also as informants spying on grandees.

questions.question: The Kannada 'Vachanas' composed by Basavanna and the 12th-century Virashaivas fundamentally challenged orthodox social hierarchy by:
options: A) Rejecting caste pollution, temple idolatry, the theory of rebirth, and orthodox taboos surrounding widow remarriage and post-puberty marriage
B) Advocating the supreme divine authority of the four Vedas and animal sacrifices
C) Banning all householders from entering monastic orders and exiling artisans
D) Promoting absolute celibacy and demanding that all followers renounce farming
questions.explanation: Virashaivas challenged the caste system, questioned rebirth, condemned temple idolatry, and encouraged widow remarriage and social equality.

questions.question: In medieval northern India, the non-conformist groups known as Naths, Jogis, and Siddhas sought ultimate spiritual realization through:
options: A) Financing maritime trading expeditions to obtain holy relics from Southeast Asia
B) Psychophysical yogic disciplines, breath regulation (pranayama), and internal meditation transcending Brahmanical caste boundaries
C) Building monumental temple towers decorated with images of royal patrons
D) Translating Greek philosophical texts into courtly Persian prose
questions.explanation: Naths and Siddhas rejected ritualism and textual scholasticism, advocating physical and yogic techniques to realize the ultimate divine.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The 'Amara-nayaka' system of military command and revenue collection in Vijayanagara was conceptually adapted from which earlier administrative framework?
options: A) The Roman centurion territorial system
B) The Persian Satrapy system of the Achaemenids
C) The Iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate
D) The Mansabdari system of Akbar
questions.explanation: The Amara-nayaka system of military chiefs assigned revenue-bearing territories was derived from the Delhi Sultanate's Iqta institution.

questions.sub_topic: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: In the religious landscape of Vijayanagara, the sacred shrine of Pampadevi honours which mythological deity?
options: A) The celestial apsara who brought celestial amrita down to the Tungabhadra basin
B) The queen consort of King Krishnadeva Raya who built the Mahanavami Dibba
C) The Buddhist goddess Tara venerated by foreign Chinese silk traders
D) The local river and tutelary goddess who performed severe austerities to wed Virupaksha (Shiva)
questions.explanation: Pampadevi was the local mother goddess who did penance on Hemakuta Hill to marry Virupaksha, the guardian deity of the kingdom.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: In Mughal agrarian economy, the fiscal term 'Jins-i Kamil' referred to:
options: A) High-value commercial cash crops such as cotton, sugarcane, and indigo that brought enhanced tax revenue to the state
B) Subsidized coarse foodgrains distributed to village serfs during seasonal droughts
C) Uncultivated pasture tracts reserved for breeding royal war stallions
D) Tolls levied on bullock caravans crossing provincial river ferries
questions.explanation: The Mughal state actively promoted Jins-i Kamil (perfect crops like cotton and sugarcane) because they yielded higher cash revenue.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Under the Mansabdari administrative structure established by Akbar, what did the numerical rank pair 'Zat' and 'Sawar' delineate?
options: A) Zat denoted land grants in barren frontier provinces, while Sawar represented ancestral urban palaces
B) Zat determined the noble's personal hierarchical standing and salary, while Sawar indicated the specific quota of mounted horsemen he was required to maintain
C) Zat represented the number of infantry foot-soldiers, while Sawar fixed the quantity of gold coins gifted at court
D) Zat specified naval warships commanded, while Sawar determined royal bodyguard duties
questions.explanation: Zat was an indicator of position in the imperial hierarchy and salary; Sawar indicated the number of horsemen the mansabdar had to maintain.

questions.sub_topic: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: What primary global economic dynamic generated the sustained influx of silver bullion into Mughal India across the 16th and 17th centuries?
options: A) The plunder of gold reserves from defeated kingdoms of the Ottoman empire
B) Direct tribute paid by East African Swahili sultans to the Agra treasury
C) Massive European commercial demand for Indian fine cotton textiles, silk, and spices paid for in silver extracted from the New World (Americas)
D) The discovery of prolific silver mines within the Gangetic plains and Chota Nagpur
questions.explanation: European trading companies purchased Indian textiles and manufactured goods with silver mined in Spanish America, injecting huge bullion into India.

questions.question: In rural Bengal under the Permanent Settlement, who were the 'Jotedars' and how did they challenge the authority of the Zamindars?
options: A) British revenue inspectors who conducted door-to-door seizures of agrarian livestock
B) Wandering tribal hunters who periodically burnt standing sugarcane crops along frontier canals
C) Traditional village astrologers who set auspicious sowing calendar schedules
D) Wealthy village-based peasant-landlords who controlled vast lands, extended local usurious credit, and deliberately instigated tenant defaults on zamindari rents
questions.explanation: Jotedars lived directly in the villages, controlled grain trade and credit, and often undermined absentee zamindars by mobilizing raiyats.

questions.question: How did the indigenous Paharia hill dwellers of the Rajmahal Hills resist British colonial efforts to convert their forested lands into settled agricultural tracts?
options: A) They withdrew into inaccessible mountain ridges and launched periodic guerrilla raids on settled lowland villages to pillage grain and cattle
B) They entered into formal military alliances with French garrisons at Chandernagore
C) They converted collectively to Anglican Christianity to secure tax-exempt tenures
D) They constructed masonry watchtowers and dug deep canal systems to flood Company outposts
questions.explanation: Paharias resisted British clearance of their sal forests by raiding plains villages, refusing to adopt settled plough agriculture.

questions.question: The Limitation Law enacted by the British administration in 1859 in western India contributed to deepening agrarian exploitation because:
options: A) It capped all agrarian interest rates at two percent per annum
B) It restricted the legal validity of loan bonds to three years, causing sahukars to compel illiterate peasants to sign new bonds turning accumulated unpaid interest into principal
C) It barred moneylenders from taking possession of peasant livestock or bullock carts
D) It mandated that all revenue defaults be settled by village panchayats rather than civil courts
questions.explanation: The 1859 Limitation Law made loan contracts valid for only three years; moneylenders exploited this by forcing ryots to sign fresh bonds compounding debt.

questions.question: In Awadh, what was the immediate socio-economic impact of the British 'Summary Settlement of 1856' upon the hereditary Taluqdars?
options: A) It elevated taluqdars to sovereign autonomous princes exempt from all imperial taxation
B) It forced taluqdars to enlist as senior commissioned officers in the Bengal Native Infantry
C) It dispossessed them of over half of their ancestral villages and dismantled their private forts and armed retainers under the dogma that they were illegitimate parasites
D) It granted taluqdars exclusive legal rights over canal irrigation networks
questions.explanation: The Summary Settlement of 1856 proceeded on the assumption that taluqdars were usurpers with no permanent stake in land, dispossessing many.

questions.question: What enigmatic traditional objects were circulated from hand to hand across villages in northern India on the eve of the uprising of 1857, creating psychological anticipation?
options: A) Copper coins bearing Mughal inscriptions and silver needles
B) Twisted peacock feathers and sanctified tulsi leaves
C) Carved wooden crosses and sandalwood rosaries
D) Chapatis and red lotus flowers
questions.explanation: The mysterious distribution of chapatis and lotus flowers passed from village to village created an atmosphere of impending upheaval before the revolt.

questions.question: During the protracted Siege of Lucknow in 1857, which British Chief Commissioner was killed inside the Residency compound by an exploding artillery shell?
options: A) Sir Henry Lawrence
B) Sir James Outram
C) Sir Colin Campbell
D) Sir Hugh Wheeler
questions.explanation: Sir Henry Lawrence died on 4 July 1857 after being fatally wounded by an artillery shell during the siege of the British Residency.

questions.question: During the anti-Rowlatt protests in April 1919, the summary arrest and deportation of which two popular national leaders in Amritsar precipitated mass public fury?
options: A) Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya
B) Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal
C) Chittaranjan Das and Bipin Chandra Pal
D) Hakim Ajmal Khan and Hasrat Mohani
questions.explanation: The arrest of leaders Dr. Satyapal and Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew on 10 April 1919 led to demonstrations, police firing, and the tragic gathering at Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.question: In his historic 'Quit India' address delivered at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay on 8 August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi proclaimed which inspiring motto?
options: A) 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'
B) 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'
C) 'Do or Die' (Karo ya Maro)
D) 'Jai Hind'
questions.explanation: Gandhi declared: 'Here is a mantra, a short one, that I give you... Do or Die. We shall either free India or die in the attempt.'

questions.question: The Cabinet Mission dispatched to India in March 1946 proposed a constitutional framework centered on:
options: A) Immediate partition into two sovereign nations with completely militarized borders
B) Direct indefinite rule by an Executive Council appointed solely by the British Crown
C) Unitary central governance with complete abolition of provincial legislatures
D) A loose three-tiered federal structure with grouped provincial sections (A, B, and C) possessing residual powers, maintaining Indian unity
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission recommended a loose federal union with weak Centre and grouped provinces to preserve the unity of India.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, which peasant leader from Andhra argued that the term 'minorities' should be understood in socio-economic terms rather than religious categories?
options: A) N.G. Ranga
B) B. Pocker Bahadur
C) Somnath Lahiri
D) Hansa Mehta
questions.explanation: Prof. N.G. Ranga argued that the real minorities of India were the poor, exploited masses, peasants, and day labourers.

questions.question: In the Constituent Assembly, who was the tribal leader from Chhota Nagpur who articulated the distinct cultural identity and historical oppression of the Adivasis?
options: A) Birsa Munda
B) Jaipal Singh
C) Sidhu Murmu
D) Thakkar Bapa
questions.explanation: Jaipal Singh spoke eloquently on behalf of tribal populations, demanding equal human status and protection against outside exploitation.

questions.question: Who served as the Chief Draughtsman of the Constituent Assembly, celebrated for his exceptional ability to draft complex constitutional clauses with legal clarity?
options: A) B.N. Rau
B) K.M. Munshi
C) S.N. Mukherjee
D) Alladi Krishnaswamy Iyer
questions.explanation: Dr. Ambedkar praised S.N. Mukherjee as the Chief Draughtsman who could put the most intricate ideas into clear legal phrasing.

questions.question: Article 356 of the Indian Constitution, granting the Union executive powers to assume provincial administration in cases of constitutional breakdown, was derived from which colonial statute?
options: A) Section 12 of the Indian Councils Act 1892
B) Section 45 of the Government of India Act 1919
C) The Rowlatt Act of 1919
D) Section 93 of the Government of India Act 1935
questions.explanation: Emergency provisions for President's Rule under Article 356 were adapted from Section 93 of the Government of India Act 1935.

questions.question: The 16th-century Rajput princess Mirabai challenged patriarchal social norms in which of the following ways?
options: A) She refused to conform to royal Rajput palace codes, recognized Krishna (Giridhar Gopal) as her supreme lord, and accepted Raidas, a leather-worker, as her spiritual guru
B) She established an armed military cavalry regiment to defend Chittor against the Mughals
C) She authored Sanskrit legal commentaries reinterpreting inheritance rules for Rajput widows
D) She traveled to Rome to debate theological doctrines with Christian cardinals
questions.explanation: Mirabai defied royal traditions, adopted the leather-worker Raidas as her preceptor, and dedicated her life to Lord Krishna.

questions.question: At which Mature Harappan site did archaeologists uncover both a ploughed agricultural field with criss-cross furrows and raised mud-brick platforms bearing fire altars?
options: A) Sutkagen Dor
B) Desalpur
C) Kalibangan
D) Mitathal
questions.explanation: Kalibangan in Rajasthan yielded evidence of an Early Harappan ploughed field and ritual mud-brick platforms containing fire altars.
